title: Papyrus CLI login with renewable Google newsroom sessions
description:
# Papyrus CLI login epic

Title: Add renewable Google newsroom login to Papyrus CLI
Type: epic; priority: 1
Suggested relationships: coordinate with PPY-58f107df-4247-4307-a6a4-1cd4896317a2 (publication BFF/Prospectus account integration) and existing Google sign-in tasks. This is separate from PPY-550d hosted procedure execution and PPY-98af local runtime hydration. Do not duplicate those implementations.

Authority/scope: Ryan requests a CLI login matching the cloned reference app, with normal newsroom identity/permissions and at least 24 hours of usable session without interactive relogin. Ryan explicitly authorized creating this NEW Kanbus epic, validating it and committing/pushing only its documentation through the normal project workflow. No implementation, credential creation, auth configuration, security change, actual login, merge or deployment is authorized. Do not bundle the separately unapproved PPY-550d comment.

## Verified reference

The matching project is **AnthusAI/Apricity**, clone `/Users/home/Projects/Apricity`, inspected HEAD `ffe8a023b0418445aa67893a52ae9e173c366d42`, origin `git@github.com:AnthusAI/Apricity.git`.

- `crates/apricity-cli/src/cloud.rs:206`: `apricity login` opens the system browser to Cognito authorize using authorization-code + PKCE S256, state and loopback `http://127.0.0.1:5181/`; code exchange occurs at the OAuth token endpoint.
- `:169,273`: refresh token stored using the keyring crate, service `apricity`, account `cognito-refresh-token` (intended OS keychain, not a plaintext project token file). No keychain values were read during this inspection.
- `:307,389`: each new API client refreshes its session; cached ID token refreshes within 60 seconds of expiry. `:410`: user ID token authenticates AppSync, preserving user ownership/groups. This is separate from Apricity's operator AWS/S3 sync path.
- `:369`: logout attempts OAuth refresh-token revocation and removes the local keychain credential.
- `web/amplify/auth/resource.ts:7` registers the CLI loopback callback; Google is federated through Cognito when configured. Source does not explicitly set refresh-token lifetime; deployed lifetime was not inspected. AWS documents a default of 30 days, but that is not a verified live Apricity setting or a measured 24-hour test.

Reference code link: https://github.com/AnthusAI/Apricity/blob/ffe8a023b0418445aa67893a52ae9e173c366d42/crates/apricity-cli/src/cloud.rs#L206

## Current Papyrus facts

Inspected reviewed checkout HEAD06c79c098c43fb4718007fc99c90795d7b6bdede and latest upstream main cf9e51f59dd3221281eae9cc5d54a8d9c9d49996. Current dispatcher/help exposes no login/logout/whoami auth command. `src/papyrus_content/graphql_http.py:26` takes IAM credentials from the AWS chain. `docs/agent-rules-detail.md:90–100` explicitly prohibits JWT/editor-login/session-cache CLI publishing. The requested product change requires a deliberate update to this contract; do not slip an undocumented JWT fallback into the existing IAM signer. Managed Lambdas continue using their roles.

`amplify/auth/prospectus-google-client.ts:5–13,52–56` explicitly describes a Google-only code+PKCE server client with one access-token-length session and no stored refresh token. Access, ID and refresh validity are configured to 60 minutes. `lib/prospectus-session.ts:16,39` stores the signed-in person and access token only; the sealed browser cookie expires with that token (`lib/prospectus-sign-in-routes.ts:148`). It cannot provide a renewable 24-hour CLI session merely by reusing that cookie. Do not scrape browser tokens or change this web client's session duration as an incidental CLI fix.

PPY-58f1 is already integrating trusted account/publication selection and fresh Prospectus grants into BFF authorization. It is not a CLI login implementation. Issue searches for login/authentication/session found Google web sign-in, BFF and restored-CMS work, but no dedicated renewable Papyrus CLI login issue. This new epic is authorized to track that distinct feature, coordinated with PPY-58f1 rather than changing its ownership.

## Proposed product contract

- `papyrus login --publication <newsroom-origin>` opens normal Google sign-in in the system browser using a supported native public OAuth client on the existing newsroom identity chain, code+PKCE S256, random state and an explicitly registered loopback callback. No embedded browser, password collection, client secret in CLI, personal AWS SSO, or new identity pool/user duplication.
- `papyrus whoami` / `papyrus auth status` reports authenticated person, issuer/publication, selected account/publication, effective newsroom capabilities, access expiry and renewable-session expiry; never displays tokens. In no-session/revoked cases return a clean actionable operator error. Noninteractive commands never open a browser themselves.
- `papyrus account list`, `papyrus account select <id>` and `papyrus publication select <id>` use the existing trusted account/publication grants. Selection is explicit when ambiguous. Store nonsecret selection metadata locally, but server rechecks current grants and tenant/resource binding for every protected action; client selection cannot grant authority. Reject cross-account/publication endpoint or issuer substitution and stale selection after a grant change.
- Support user-authenticated CLI editorial commands through the same supported server authorization surface as the signed-in newsroom. For existing AppSync userPool operations, use the documented Cognito user-token transport explicitly rather than IAM fallback; where Prospectus/BFF authorization is the authoritative surface, use that verified server route and its fresh grant checks. The implementation owner must settle the exact supported request boundary with PPY-58f1 before coding: a user token must never bypass account/publication grants merely because a legacy GraphQL model accepts an editor group. This is an integration gate, not permission to invent an ad hoc gateway or new authorizer.
- Keep operator/infrastructure AWS commands explicitly IAM-backed and existing Lambda role auth unchanged. No automatic switch from a rejected user session to broader IAM authority. CLI user-auth mode and IAM mode must be legible in status/log metadata (without secrets).
- Authenticate requests as the normal newsroom person and preserve their actual permissions. Record agent-produced content as ChatGPT/agent where applicable; user authentication does not transform agent research into a human editorial label or decision. Do not silently expand grants.

## Session and token design

Target **at least24hours usable session after login**, across CLI process restarts and M1 sleep/resume, with network/service availability and no intervening revocation or authorization removal. This means renewable session lifetime of at least24hours plus a tested boundary margin; it does not mean an irrevocable24hour access token. Configure an explicit renewable-session lifetime greater than24hours with a tested boundary margin; settle the exact policy value with the identity owner rather than assume a default. Keep access/ID expiry short (proposed at most60minutes). Set/verify these values explicitly rather than relying on defaults. Confirm policy and identity registration compatibility before changing any app client. Other web sessions need not be extended.

Store only renewable secret material in the OS secure credential store, scoped by issuer, native client, subject and publication/account binding; metadata/cache files contain no bearer or refresh secrets. On M1 use macOS Keychain through a maintained Python-compatible backend (Papyrus remains Python-first). If secure storage is unavailable or locked, fail visibly; no plaintext fallback to repo/.env/config files or logs. Never inspect/export the user's existing keychain entries during implementation tests.

Cache short-lived token material in process memory. Refresh ahead of expiry with clock skew; on restart obtain a fresh user token from the stored renewable session. Handle refresh-token rotation and atomically replace the saved refresh token if the provider returns one; serialize concurrent refreshes for the same session to avoid invalidating another process. Retain the old credential on transient timeout/429/5xx and report/retry boundedly; clear/relogin only on a confirmed invalid_grant/revoked/expired session. Do not blindly retry a mutation after an uncertain network outcome. Reuse operation idempotency/audit semantics.

Use the correct token type for the declared API: Apricity currently uses an ID token for AppSync; a BFF access-token verifier may require an access token with a particular audience/scope. Verify issuer, client/audience and token_use server-side. Do not treat unverified decoded claims as authorization. Refresh must not reset an absolute expiry beyond server policy. An app/client allowed redirect and backend accepted issuer/client registration are required implementation inputs; no new registration/settings are changed in this design task.

## Logout and revocation

`papyrus logout` attempts revocation of the selected refresh session, then always deletes its local secrets and selection cache. Return distinct status if remote revocation could not be confirmed while offline; do not say remote logout succeeded. `--all` would require a separately defined explicit global-signout choice, not silent signout of other devices. Tests must establish actual server behavior for revoked credentials and already-issued access tokens; do not promise immediate invalidation of every self-contained token without enforcement. Short access expiry bounds residual validity where applicable. Session renewal cannot restore a revoked grant or bypass publication selection checks.

## Implementation plan after scope approval

1. Agree normal newsroom API boundary with PPY-58f1 and explicitly replace the IAM-only CLI policy for supported user-facing editorial operations; leave operator/Lambda IAM rules intact. Document trust/issuer/native-client registration and exact publication-discovery metadata. Decide refresh lifetime and secure storage behavior before configuration work.
2. Add Python session/auth module and login/status/logout command surface, with mock-provider BDD first. Add external-browser PKCE loopback handling, timeout/cancel/state/error handling and keychain abstraction. Use local fake OAuth/keychain services in tests; never real tokens.
3. Add renewable user transport to supported editorial operations and thread it through Tactus child processes using a secure session handle/normal credential resolver, not raw tokens in argv, logs or inherited all-purpose secret environment. An auth child process must select the same publication/identity binding; no automatic personal AWS assumption. Cover API calls, attachment reads/uploads and actual permission failure handling.
4. Add account/publication selection using real backend authorization integration, fresh grant recheck and concurrency-safe session selection. Reuse existing user claims/capabilities rather than maintaining a second permissions database.
5. Verify a real approved24hour session, clock-boundary simulation, expiry/rotation/revocation and user-permission parity; then update docs/skill guidance. Deployment/configuration/release remain separately authorized work. This feature does not implement a hosted Tactus worker, repair the Run now placeholder, or by itself prove any research execution.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed Gherkin)

Feature: Renewable normal-user CLI session

Scenario: Google login without an AWS operator session
  Given an authorized newsroom user and a configured publication-native OAuth client
  And no AWS SSO/profile credentials are available
  When the user runs papyrus login and completes normal Google sign-in
  Then the CLI identifies that person and their current newsroom permissions
  And secrets are saved only in the secure credential store

Scenario: Renew beyond24hours without interaction
  Given an unrevoked renewable session with authorized publication access
  When time passes beyond24hours and access tokens expire across CLI restarts and sleep
  Then a protected supported command silently renews and succeeds without opening a browser
  And short-lived tokens are renewed rather than extended to24hours

Scenario: Grant or publication selection changes
  Given a session bound to account A and publication P
  When access to P is removed or selection changes while an operation is pending
  Then stale/cross-tenant work is denied before any protected mutation
  And no broader IAM fallback or guessed tenant is used

Scenario: Concurrent refresh and transient failure
  Given two CLI processes share the same renewable session
  When token rotation or a transient provider failure occurs
  Then refresh replacement is atomic and bounded
  And a transient error does not erase an otherwise usable session
  And an uncertain mutation is not replayed blindly

Scenario: Logout and revocation
  Given a signed-in CLI session
  When papyrus logout runs
  Then local credentials are removed even if the network is unavailable
  And remote revocation success or uncertainty is reported accurately
  And confirmed revoked/expired credentials require interactive login rather than looping

Scenario: Agent attribution stays honest
  Given an authenticated person authorizes agent reporting
  When the CLI records research notes or references
  Then request identity and content author/agent provenance remain distinct
  And no human label or approval is invented

## Evidence and verification limits

This is a source-backed design, not implementation or live-auth proof. No reference app login, keychain retrieval, provider call, settings change, new token, implementation or deployment was performed. Kanbus epic filing and its documentation-only commit/push are separately authorized by Ryan at10:33UTC. Apricity's clone already has other agents' Kanbus changes; all were preserved. Existing local PPY-550d comment remains uncommitted and untouched.

Official references checked:
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8252/ (native external browser/PKCE flow)
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-using-the-refresh-token.html (renewal/session lifetime)
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-revocation.html (session revocation semantics)
- https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/04/amazon-cognito-refresh-token-rotation/ (rotation support)


Acceptance evidence must report four separate results: configured token/session values from reviewed code/configuration; simulated-clock expiry/renewal/concurrency/revocation tests; an actual elapsed >=24hour unattended test with timestamped redacted receipts including process restart/sleep; and end-to-end authorization/tenant parity. Configuration and simulation alone must never be called a successful elapsed24hour test. No such live24hour result exists yet.
